opening_question_spark: Can a cat be alive and dead at once? I wonder while feeding chickens.
book_transition: So I grab the physics book nearby.
cta: Like and subscribe to grow more questions.
body: In 1935, Erwin Schrödinger imagined a sealed box with a cat.
Inside, a radioactive atom may decay or stay unchanged.
Decay triggers a mechanism that releases poison.
No decay means the cat survives.
Quantum theory can represent both atomic possibilities in superposition.
That links the cat to both possible fates.
Schrödinger designed the absurd scenario to expose the measurement problem.
optional_closing: The cat was never a real experiment.
full_narration: Can a cat be alive and dead at once? I wonder while feeding chickens. So I grab the physics book nearby. In 1935, Erwin Schrödinger imagined a sealed box with a cat. Inside, a radioactive atom may decay or stay unchanged. Decay triggers a mechanism that releases poison. No decay means the cat survives. Quantum theory can represent both atomic possibilities in superposition. That links the cat to both possible fates. Schrödinger designed the absurd scenario to expose the measurement problem. The cat was never a real experiment. Like and subscribe to grow more questions.
